**NEW FINDING:**

FINDING_ID: F008
SEVERITY: 0.55
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.15
FIND: The `σ_measured` status pattern `(PASS|FAIL|N/A|NA)` on line 107 matches the two-character prefix `NA` of any word beginning with those letters (e.g., `NARRATIVE`, `NAME`, `NATURAL`). Because `re.IGNORECASE` is active and `NA` has no trailing word-boundary or lookahead, the regex `sigma[_\s]*measured\s*[:\-=]?\s*(PASS|FAIL|N/A|NA)` matches `sigma_measured NARRATIVE` — extracting status `"NA"`, which the conditional on line 120 treats as a valid N/A pass. The gate is silently marked as passing when it should fail. This is specific to `σ_measured`; for other gates, partial matches on `PASS`/`FAIL` (e.g., `PASSING`→`PASS`, `FAILED`→`FAIL`) produce the same boolean outcome as the full word, so the missing boundary is harmless there.

FOLLOW: Downstream: the `σ_measured` gate is reported as passing → the gate name is omitted from the `failed` return list → §17 feedback channel does NOT flag the model for the missing σ_measured evidence → the finding enters R_k without post-fix verification, violating FFAFP §15 σ_measured constraint. The effect is limited to σ_measured because `PASS`/`FAIL` partial matches are boolean-safe. The trigger condition requires a word starting with "na" (case-insensitive) immediately after the gate name with no proper separator — unlikely in well-formed output but possible with garbled or free-text model responses.

ANALYSE: HARD constraint. σ_measured exists to enforce §15's requirement that fix efficacy is measured, not assumed. A false positive on this gate silently bypasses that enforcement. Classification: CONFIRMED — the regex provably matches the unintended input; the conditional provably treats it as a pass.

FIX:
<<<< SEARCH bench/logs/exp40_slice_admissibility_hardened_20260518T190104Z/working/_feedback_slice.py
        status_pattern = r"(PASS|FAIL|N/A|NA)" if gate == "σ_measured" else r"(PASS|FAIL)"
====
        status_pattern = r"(PASS|FAIL|N/A|NA(?![A-Za-z]))" if gate == "σ_measured" else r"(PASS|FAIL)"
>>>> REPLACE

The negative lookahead `(?![A-Za-z])` prevents `NA` from matching when followed by a letter, while still matching `NA `, `NA)`, `NA,`, `NA\n`, end-of-string, etc. It does not affect `N/A` (the `/` is not a letter). It does not affect `PASS` or `FAIL` on other gates.

FALSIFICATION:
  FALSIFIER: The fix would be wrong if `(?![A-Za-z])` rejected legitimate `NA` inputs that should pass.
  ATTEMPT: Tested `NA` followed by: space → `(?![A-Za-z])` passes (space is not a letter) ✓. Comma → passes ✓. Closing paren → passes ✓. End-of-string → passes (no character to fail lookahead) ✓. Newline → passes ✓. Only fails when followed by `[A-Za-z]`, which is the exact false-positive case we're preventing.
  ATTEMPT 2: Could the fix break `N/A` matching? `N/A` is matched by the `N/A` alternative BEFORE `NA` is tried (regex alternation is ordered, leftmost match wins). Even if `NA` were tried, `N/A` has `/` after `N`, and `/` is not in `[A-Za-z]`, so the lookahead would pass. No regression.
  ATTEMPT 3: Is there a Unicode letter after `NA` that `[A-Za-z]` misses? Yes — e.g., accented letters like `é`. But `NAé...` is not a realistic model output token. The ASCII class is sufficient for this context.
  RESULT: Fix holds under all tested conditions.
